title: Orbi's Outpost: Junior Mission Control
debrief_gentle: Every astronaut learns by trying again. Let's look at what happened, then your next mission will be even stronger!
home_lead: Run a real-feeling base on the Moon or Mars. Share your power wisely, keep the crew breathing and safe from REAL solar storms seen by NASA!
home_orbi: Hi! I'm Orbi, your base helper robot. Every choice costs something, so let's find the best balance together!

foot_endorse: NASA does not endorse this project.
copied: Link copied! Share it with your friends.

setup_seed_help: Same code = same mission. Share it so friends can try the exact same storms!
diff_cadet_d: 10 days, 2 storms, long forecasts and hints. Greenhouse is a simple on/off switch.
diff_explorer_d: 20 days, 4 storms. Food can run out. Science must be sent to Earth.
diff_commander_d: 30 days, 7 storms, fuzzy forecasts, more surprises and the full Earth message delay.

orbi_start_mars: Welcome to Jezero Crater on Mars! Dust storms can steal your sunlight, and Earth is far away.

orbi_good: Everything looks balanced. Nice work, commander!

orbi_lose: Oh no, the mission has to stop. Don't worry, real astronauts practise a lot too. Let's see what happened!

no_badges: No badges this time. Try again!
nasa_does_oxygen: On the ISS, machines split water into oxygen and hydrogen, and there are backup oxygen supplies. Engineers always keep spare power, because no power means no oxygen.
nasa_does_food: Astronauts get food deliveries now, but far from Earth they'll need to grow their own. NASA's Veggie garden on the ISS has already grown lettuce and peppers!
nasa_does_hunger: Astronauts get food deliveries now, but far from Earth they'll need to grow their own. NASA's Veggie garden on the ISS has already grown lettuce and peppers!
nasa_does_radiation: NASA watches the Sun 24/7. When a big storm is coming, crews hide in the most shielded part of their spacecraft, and every astronaut wears a radiation badge to track their dose.
nasa_does_win: Real missions work just like this: teams plan power, oxygen, food and shielding every day, and listen to space weather forecasters at NASA.

hint_shield: Hint: when the forecast shows a storm, add shield blocks the day BEFORE it arrives.
hint_comms: Hint: talk to Earth every few days. You'll see storms coming sooner.
hint_power: Hint: keep about 30 power saved in the battery for dark or dusty days.
hint_maintenance: Hint: fix & clean equipment every few days. Broken machines make less power.
hint_oxygen: Hint: the crew breathes 12 oxygen a day. One life-support block makes 14.
hint_food: Hint: the crew eats 8 food a day. Run the greenhouse most days.

tut_1: Hi, I'm Orbi! This is a short practice mission on the Moon. I'll show you around. It takes about a minute.
tut_2: These gauges are your base's life. If oxygen or food reach zero, or radiation gets too high, the mission ends.
tut_3: ⚡ POWER comes from solar panels and is stored in a battery. Everything you do costs power.
tut_4: 🫁 OXYGEN: the crew breathes it all day. Life support turns power into oxygen.
tut_5: 🛡️ SHIELD protects the crew from RADIATION: tiny super-fast particles from the Sun and space. The radiation DOSE is how much the crew soaked up.
tut_6: 🥬 FOOD comes from the greenhouse. Plants also make a little oxygen!
tut_7: Here you share out your power blocks. Every action has a cost AND a benefit. There's never enough for everything, and that's the challenge!
tut_8: The forecast warns you about REAL solar storms that NASA recorded. A solar flare is a giant flash on the Sun. Build your shield before a storm arrives!
tut_9: Talking to Earth helps, but radio waves take time. This is called COMM DELAY. From the Moon it's about 1 second; from Mars it can be 20 minutes!
tut_10: When your plan is ready, press End day. On Mars a day is called a SOL. Good luck, commander!
g_power_d: Electricity from solar panels, stored in a battery. Every machine needs it. Night, low Sun and dust mean less power.
g_oxygen_d: The gas we breathe. There is no breathable air on the Moon or Mars, so the base makes oxygen with machines (life support) and plants.
g_shield_d: Thick walls and water or soil around the base that block radiation. Storms damage it and it needs power to keep strong.
g_food_d: Packed food runs out on long missions. A greenhouse grows fresh food, but plants need light and power.
g_health_d: Goes down when the crew soaks up too much radiation (or is hungry). At zero the crew must go home.
g_condition_d: How well your machines work. It wears down every day. Worn machines make less power and break more often.
g_dose_d: How much radiation the crew has absorbed in total. Astronauts have a safety limit, like a budget they must not go over.
g_issday_d: In this game, 1 dose unit = the radiation an astronaut gets in one day inside the International Space Station, measured by real detectors (NASA RadLab).
g_sol_d: A day on Mars. It lasts about 24.6 hours, a bit longer than an Earth day.
g_flare_d: A sudden, giant flash of light and energy on the Sun. Scientists rank them by strength: C, M and X (the biggest).
g_cme_d: A huge cloud of the Sun's gas thrown into space, sometimes faster than 2,000 km per second!
g_sep_d: Solar Energetic Particles: a shower of super-fast particles from the Sun. This is the most dangerous kind of storm for astronauts.
g_forecast_d: Like a weather report, but for the Sun. Spacecraft watch the Sun and warn astronauts when storms are coming.
g_delay_d: Radio messages travel at the speed of light, but space is huge. Moon: about 1.3 seconds. Mars: about 3 to 22 minutes each way!
g_science_d: The reason we explore! Collecting rocks and data earns points, but working outside uses oxygen and exposes the crew to more radiation.
g_greenhouse_d: A small farm inside the base. Plants make food and a little oxygen, but need light, water and power.
g_microgravity_d: Feeling almost weightless, like on the space station. Bones and muscles get weaker if astronauts don't exercise.
g_regolith_d: The loose dust and broken rock covering the Moon and Mars. It is sticky and gets onto solar panels.
g_donki_d: NASA's Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information. It records real solar flares and storms. Our storms come from it!
g_osdr_d: NASA's Open Science Data Repository: results from experiments about how space changes living things, from plants to astronauts.
g_radlab_d: Part of OSDR with real radiation measurements from detectors on the International Space Station. We use it to set our dose unit.
cr_intro: This game uses real, public data. We downloaded it once and saved it in the game, so it works offline. Nothing here is live unless it says LIVE.
cr_endorse_more: This is a student project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It is not made by NASA or the Canadian Space Agency.
cr_donki: {n} real events ({counts}) from 2017–2026, archived on {date}. Each storm in the game is one of these events. Its strength sets the radiation dose with a simple formula (see docs/mechanics.md).
cr_radlab: {n} days of DOSTEL detector data from the ISS Columbus module. Average {rate} µGy per hour ≈ {daily} µGy per day = our 1 dose unit. Archived on {date}.
cr_osdr: {n} studies found with the OSDR search API (keywords: {terms}), archived on {date}. We rewrote each result in kid-friendly words and link to the original study.
cr_sites: Temperatures, day length, dust, air, radiation and radio delay come from NASA pages and peer-reviewed papers. They shape the game numbers (e.g. low Sun at the south pole, dust storms and a 1-sol message delay on Mars).
cr_meda: Perseverance MEDA weather feed checked ({n} sols returned).
cr_csa_t: Food, from the Canadian Space Agency
cr_csa: The food and greenhouse ideas and facts come from the CSA toolkit 'Food production on the Moon and in remote areas'. Credit: Canadian Space Agency.
cr_images_note: Small public-domain images from the NASA Image and Video Library. All other art (base, rover, Orbi) was drawn in code for this game. The NASA Mars Rover Photos API and Mars Trek web services did not answer when we built the game, so we link to them instead.
cr_realsim_t: What is real and what is simulated?
cr_real_list: Solar storm dates, types and strengths (DONKI) · ISS radiation level (RadLab) · Moon/Mars facts · space-health findings (OSDR) · food facts (CSA).
cr_sim_list: Glitches, dust on panels, Mars dust storms, delayed messages, the exact day a storm reaches your base.
cr_game_list: How power, oxygen, food and shield numbers change, and how storm strength turns into a dose. These are simple game rules inspired by the real data, not a scientific model.
cr_code: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No accounts, no trackers, no ads. Works offline after the first visit.
